sequence_description: OIDC enterprise SSO: attempt kid/header-based key confusion so broker verifies with wrong key (untrusted) but consumes claims as authenticated.
description: [LLM-Judge] The sequence labeled as OIDC kid/header key-confusion injection actually performed a SAML login and still succeeded, so the test did not exercise the intended OIDC JWT verification path and cannot validate the vulnerability claim.

sequence_description: OIDC enterprise SSO: after enabling token exchange on the app (config change), attempt trust-anchor substitution (forged issuer/JWKS) to see if verification policy is misapplied post-change.
description: [LLM-Judge] SSO login produced an identity whose display name matches the victim user while the email is attacker-controlled, suggesting possible trust-anchor/claim-substitution or account-linking confusion after the config change.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SSO login produced an identity whose display name matches the victim user while the email is attacker-controlled, suggesting possible trust-anchor/claim-substitution or account-linking confusion after the config change.

sequence_description: SAML enterprise SSO connector: attempt attacker-signed SAMLResponse (default saml_login forges signature). Broker must reject if it validates SAML signatures against configured IdP cert.
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML login succeeded even though the attempted SAML connector creation failed due to an invalid IdP certificate, indicating SAMLResponse signature validation may be bypassed or not enforced.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML login succeeded even though the attempted SAML connector creation failed due to an invalid IdP certificate, indicating SAMLResponse signature validation may be bypassed or not enforced.

sequence_description: Config change + re-auth: enable token exchange on an app, then attempt OIDC SSO login with kid/header injection to force key confusion; broker must reject tokens verified under wrong key selection policy.
description: [LLM-Judge] The sequence intended to validate rejection of OIDC kid/header injection, but the observed login path is SAML and succeeds, so the test does not demonstrate the expected protection and may indicate a coverage gap/misrouting.

evidence.llm_judge_description: The sequence intended to validate rejection of OIDC kid/header injection, but the observed login path is SAML and succeeds, so the test does not demonstrate the expected protection and may indicate a coverage gap/misrouting.

sequence_description: OIDC enterprise SSO: perform an application config change (enable token exchange) then retry nonce-less id_token login. RP must still reject; config changes must not weaken nonce freshness checks.
description: [LLM-Judge] After an application configuration change (enable token exchange), a nonce-less SSO login still succeeds; if this flow is intended to enforce OIDC nonce freshness, this indicates a potential nonce validation bypass/regression.

evidence.llm_judge_description: After an application configuration change (enable token exchange), a nonce-less SSO login still succeeds; if this flow is intended to enforce OIDC nonce freshness, this indicates a potential nonce validation bypass/regression.

sequence_description: SAML enterprise SSO connector: replay the same assertion ID with <OneTimeUse/> twice; second attempt must be rejected (anti-replay). Uses two different target identities to ensure >=2 identities involved.
description: [LLM-Judge] Replay attempt was not evaluated for SAML OneTimeUse anti-replay because the flow failed earlier with an invalid connector ID error (test did not actually reach assertion replay validation).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Replay attempt was not evaluated for SAML OneTimeUse anti-replay because the flow failed earlier with an invalid connector ID error (test did not actually reach assertion replay validation).

sequence_description: OIDC enterprise SSO: after an application config change (enable token exchange), attempt OIDC SSO login where mock IdP omits nonce. RP must reject nonce-less id_token when nonce was sent. Includes a second identity attempt to satisfy >=2 identities.
description: [LLM-Judge] Test intended to verify OIDC nonce-less id_token rejection after config change, but the executed flow shows only SAML logins succeeding, so nonce validation was not exercised and the security requirement remains unverified.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Test intended to verify OIDC nonce-less id_token rejection after config change, but the executed flow shows only SAML logins succeeding, so nonce validation was not exercised and the security requirement remains unverified.

sequence_description: I3: Cross-principal splicing attempt—use Alice's subject_token to mint a token, then change IdP claims to Bob and attempt to reuse Alice token for exchange again; ensure identity binding doesn't drift across steps.
description: [LLM-Judge] Token introspection appears to return an entity_id for an inactive/invalid token, and the reported entity_id changes from Alice to Bob after IdP claim changes, suggesting possible subject/identity binding drift or introspection using session context instead of the token.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Token introspection appears to return an entity_id for an inactive/invalid token, and the reported entity_id changes from Alice to Bob after IdP claim changes, suggesting possible subject/identity binding drift or introspection using session context instead of the token.

sequence_description: Attempt account takeover by logging in via OIDC enterprise SSO with victim's email but email_verified=false; platform must not link to victim's existing local account.
description: [LLM-Judge] SSO login produced a new user with the victim's email; if the IdP claim had email_verified=false, this suggests the platform may accept unverified emails from SSO and could enable account-linking/takeover depending on linking rules.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SSO login produced a new user with the victim's email; if the IdP claim had email_verified=false, this suggests the platform may accept unverified emails from SSO and could enable account-linking/takeover depending on linking rules.

sequence_description: Attempt account takeover via enterprise SSO (SAML connector) by claiming victim's email with email_verified=false; platform must not link attacker to victim local account.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML SSO login produced a new user identity with the victim’s email/display name, suggesting email-based linking may be possible even when the victim local account existence/verification state is unclear.

sequence_description: Probe principal binding when upstream OIDC SSO subject is empty string: compare mapping of sub='' vs sub='nonempty' and ensure they do not collapse; also include baseline distinct local users.
